name: NavSense
tagline: Smart gloves that turn walking directions into vibration patterns, with a voice agent for planning and siren alerts.
problem: Spoken directions compete with street noise and screens pull eyes off the path, which is risky for blind, low-vision, Deaf and hard-of-hearing pedestrians.
solution: Two gloves with microcontrollers connect over Bluetooth Low Energy to a mobile app that fetches a route, splits it into steps and assigns each manoeuvre a distinct vibration pattern with consistent timing. A voice agent handles destination, travel mode and rerouting; an on-device audio model detects sirens and tells the wearer to pause.
demo_moment: Team-described: a turn arrives as a vibration in the left or right hand, and a siren nearby makes both gloves signal stop.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Took third place overall among 124 submissions.
Serves two groups with one device: people who cannot rely on sight and people who cannot rely on sound.
Adds a safety layer beyond navigation: siren detection pauses the route.
Wearable hardware that judges can put on makes the accessibility claim tangible.

lessons: An accessibility device that judges can wear turns empathy into a demo.
